question: Carbon forms many compounds because of:

options.text: High atomic mass and large size

solution:
The correct answer is __**Catenation and tetravalency**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Catenation** is the unique property of **Carbon** atoms to form bonds with other atoms of carbon, resulting in the formation of large molecules, long chains, branched chains, or cyclic structures. This ability allows carbon to form an almost infinite variety of compounds.
 
• **Tetravalency** refers to the fact that carbon has **four valence electrons** in its outermost shell. This allows it to form **four covalent bonds** with other carbon atoms or atoms of other monovalent elements like **Hydrogen**, **Oxygen**, **Nitrogen**, and **Sulfur**. ***Hence, the statement regarding catenation and tetravalency is correct.***
 
• The **bond strength** of carbon-carbon bonds is exceptionally high, which makes the resulting compounds very stable. This stability is due to the **small size** of the carbon atom, which enables the nucleus to hold the shared pairs of electrons firmly.
